architecture/extension-lifecycle.title: Extension lifecycle
architecture/extension-lifecycle.description: An extension registers domain-owned components, actions, schemas, and routes through the platform's generic catalog and integration points.

architecture/package-boundaries.title: Package boundaries
architecture/package-boundaries.description: Noname keeps generic platform capability separate from vertical business semantics and extension-owned presentation.

concepts/documents-and-layouts.title: Documents and layouts
concepts/documents-and-layouts.description: Documents are the platform's content and page composition boundary. Layout specifications describe what the client renders without placing domain-specific business rules in the generic shell.

concepts/evidence-and-provenance.title: Evidence and provenance
concepts/evidence-and-provenance.description: Noname uses immutable Evidence records and typed links to make important domain outcomes auditable without making the generic server domain Commerce-specific.

concepts/machines-and-xstate.title: Machines and XState
concepts/machines-and-xstate.description: Noname machine definitions are JSON-compatible data. XState is the sole transition authority.

concepts/seeding.title: Seeding and fixtures
concepts/seeding.description: Seeding creates deterministic environments. Fixtures provide pure reusable data. Domain-specific test doubles remain close to the domain that owns them.

concepts/system-overview.title: System overview
concepts/system-overview.description: Noname is a declarative full-stack platform. A specification can drive content, UI, backend machines, capabilities, and integrations while domain-owned verticals provide business meaning.

history/audit-reports.description: The repository-wide documentation audit is preserved as dated evidence:

history/implementation-records.title: Implementation records
history/implementation-records.description: Implementation records preserve what changed, how it was tested, and what was known at the time.

history/overview.title: History and audit records
history/overview.description: This section keeps the engineering record separate from the learning path.

how-to/create-an-extension.title: Create an extension
how-to/create-an-extension.description: How-to guide · Start from an existing vertical or extension example.

how-to/verify-a-checkout.title: Verify a checkout
how-to/verify-a-checkout.description: How-to guide · Exercise the reliability path without treating a plan as proof.

index.title: Noname documentation
index.description: Noname is an AI-native, declarative full-stack platform. Describe what you want, represent it as a spec, and execute it across UI, backend machines, integrations, and vertical extensions.

reference/api/capabilities.title: Capabilities API
reference/api/capabilities.description: Capabilities are generic server execution boundaries. Commerce checkout is a vertical-owned capability exposed through the generic capability route.

reference/api/evidence.title: Evidence API
reference/api/evidence.description: Current generic read contract. OpenAPI generation will replace hand-maintained request/response details when the route schema export is available.

reference/api/machines.title: Machines API
reference/api/machines.description: The machine API loads normalized JSON definitions, executes XState transitions through ephemeral actors, and persists the resulting state and context.

reference/index.title: Reference
reference/index.description: Reference pages document exact contracts. They are intentionally compact and should be generated from schemas where possible.

reference/permissions.title: Permissions reference
reference/permissions.description: Permissions are tenant-aware and enforced through the platform identity and authorization boundaries. Domain UI should request generic permission/catalog capabilities rather than reimplementing authorization logic.
